title: Hospital Visits and New Babies
short: Ask before visiting, keep it short, stay home if you are sick, wash your hands, and offer help with meals or errands rather than asking to hold the baby.
trouble: Learners drop in unannounced or stay for hours. New parents and patients need rest more than company.

blocks.html: Visiting someone in the hospital, or a family with a new baby, uses the same care as visiting the bereaved: short visits and specific help. The person you are visiting needs rest more than company.
Ask before visiting, keep it short, stay home if you are sick, wash your hands, and offer help with meals or errands rather than asking to hold the baby.

Patients and new parents are tired, and their days are full of care, feedings and doctors' visits. Asking first lets them choose a good time, or say not yet. A short visit gives cheer without draining them. Staying home when you are sick and washing your hands are widely agreed ways to protect someone recovering or a newborn. Help with meals or errands lightens their load in a way a visit alone cannot.

messages.text: She's here! 7 lb 2 oz, and we're all doing well. Home on Thursday.

choices.text: Congratulations! Can I come over tomorrow to meet her?
choices.why: The day after coming home is often exhausting. Let the parents choose the time.

choices.text: Congratulations to all of you! I'd love to drop off dinner one night next week. Which night is best?
choices.why: Warm, with a specific offer, and the parents choose the time.

choices.text: Send pictures! When can I hold her?
choices.why: Holding the baby is the parents' offer to make, not the visitor's request.

blocks.title: A hospital visit
blocks.q: Nora's friend James had surgery and is in the hospital. What should she do?
steps: She texts first: "Would you like a visitor this week?"
If he says yes, she visits for a short time and checks the hospital's visiting rules.
She brings a book or a card, and she stays home if she has a cold.
blocks.a: Ask first, visit briefly, stay home if sick.

blocks.title: Meeting the baby
blocks.q: Leo visits his sister and her new baby. What helps most?
steps: He washes his hands when he arrives.
He brings a meal, offers to do the dishes or run an errand, and stays a short time.
He waits for the parents to offer to let him hold the baby.
blocks.a: Clean hands, practical help, a short stay.

blocks.html: Dropping in unannounced or staying for hours. New parents and patients need rest more than company. Quick check: did they choose the time, and will you leave before they tire?
